questions.explain: Cosine measures the angle between vectors, ignoring length — documents saying the same thing in different amounts of detail point the same direction, so discarding magnitude removes noise.
options: It is the only metric VECTOR_DISTANCE supports
Most text embedding models produce vectors whose magnitude carries little semantic meaning, and cosine ignores vector length, measuring only the angle
Cosine distance is always exactly zero for identical documents
Text models output sparse vectors that Euclidean distance cannot handle
questions.q: Why is cosine the default metric for text embeddings?

questions.explain: The chapter notes the convention — VECTOR_DISTANCE returns distance where 0 means identical — so cosine similarity, the thing humans talk about, is 1 − distance.
options: Take the square root of the distance
Multiply by −1 and divide by the dimension count
Cosine similarity equals the distance itself
Compute 1 − distance, which ranges from 1 (identical direction) through 0 (orthogonal) to −1 (opposite)
questions.q: In SQL Server, VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', ...) returns a distance. How do you convert it to the cosine similarity humans talk about?

questions.explain: 'dot' returns the negative dot product; negate it in the SELECT list for a human-readable score but always ORDER BY the raw distance ascending — sorting the negated score ascending silently inverts recommendations.
options: The negative dot product, so the 'smaller distance = more similar' convention holds; ORDER BY the raw distance ascending
The plain dot product, so you must ORDER BY descending
The dot product divided by the vector lengths
A random score used only for testing

questions.explain: The metric in the index, the query, and the model must all agree; a mismatch makes the query 'correct' in that it returns rows, but silently slow with no error and no warning.
options: The query errors out with a metric mismatch exception
The index automatically converts the stored vectors to Euclidean space
The optimizer cannot use the index for ranking — it falls back to a full scan, and latency jumps from milliseconds to seconds with no error and no warning
Results are identical because all metrics produce the same ranking
questions.q: Your vector index was built WITH (METRIC = 'cosine') but a query calls VECTOR_DISTANCE('euclidean', ...). What happens?

questions.explain: If you normalize all embeddings at ingest time, cosine distance and L2 distance rank identically; without normalization the choice genuinely changes results.
options: They are unrelated metrics
Euclidean always returns zero on normalized vectors
Cosine cannot be computed on normalized vectors
They produce identical rankings — the two are monotonically related — so either metric gives the same top-k results
questions.q: For unit-normalized (L2-normalized) vectors, how do cosine and Euclidean distance compare?
